Lemma
[lifts of finite-length curves are relatively compact]

↗ lem:dc-ch7-3-3-length-expansion ↗ thm:dc-ch7-2-8 ↗ def:dc-ch7-2-4

1. ch7:3.3Let $f:M\to N$ expand the metric ($|df_p(v)|\ge |v|$ for all $p,v$), and let $M$ be a complete Riemannian manifold. Then for every piecewise differentiable curve $\bar c:[a,b]\to M$ whose image $f\circ \bar c$ has finite length, and for every $t\in [a,b]$, \[ d\big(\bar c(a),\bar c(t)\big)\ \le \ \ell (f\circ \bar c), \] so $\bar c(t)$ lies in the closed metric ball $\bar B\big(\bar c(a),\ell (f\circ \bar c)\big)$. Consequently the whole image $\bar c([a,b])$ is contained in a single compact subset $K\subset M$.
Proof

↗ lem:dc-ch7-3-3-length-expansion ↗ thm:dc-ch7-2-8 \sketch Apply the length estimate to each restriction of the lifted curve. Every lift point lies in the closed ball of radius $\ell (f\circ \bar c)$ about its initial point, which is compact by Hopf–Rinow.

□
